chapter_theme: The futile garb (அவ வேடம்): those who put on the ascetic's guise for food and show do not reach Siva's feet; the land suffers when the ignorant wear it, so the ruler should correct his people and strip the base of it; false austerity leads to hell, and garb saves only those who have come to know.
structure_note: Two verses on the pretender and the harm he does the land (1655, 1656), two on the ruler's duty to set the land right and weed out the false (1657, 1658), and two weighing false against true austerity and garb (1659, 1660).

1655.reading: Fools who put on guises and frighten people so as to eat their food in pomp: dance, sing, weep, wail and search as you will, you will not see Siva's feet.
1655.nuance: வெருட்டிடும் (who frighten) suggests ascetics who overawe householders into feeding them. The dancing, singing and weeping of line 3 are the outward marks of devotion; the verse says that performed for show they find nothing.

1656.reading: If men without knowledge wear the garb in the land, do base things and live by begging, the land's honour and good decay and famine comes; to make the base put off the garb is a joy.
1656.nuance: The harm is public, not only the pretender's own: the land loses its standing and suffers famine. Who is to strip the garb is left unsaid; the next verses and 241 put it on the ruler.

1657.reading: Joy and sorrow in a land come to it from the good and bad deeds of its people; so it is said that if the ruler looks into it every day and sets the people of his land right, the world will flourish.
1657.nuance: இறை here is the king, not the Lord, though the word allows both. The verse makes the king answerable for his subjects' conduct, not only for his own; in this chapter that means dealing with false ascetics.

1658.reading: Men of low birth put on the garb to rise, men of the right line put it on to become gods; those who became ruined, base men of a blameworthy line, the outcast ones, are to be weeded out.
1658.nuance: Every line turns on a compound with குலம் (இழி, வழி, பழி, கழி), and their sense is unsure: வழிகுலம் may be 'those of the proper line' or 'those who follow the way', and சண்டர் may mean the fierce or the outcast. களையப்பட்டோர் (weeded out) echoes the ruler's duty of 1657; whether the verse ranks garb-wearers by birth or uses birth words for conduct can't be fixed from the Tamil.

1659.reading: Those who practise false austerity go to hell, and if they do not become men of merit, false and true austerity alike are things to be undergone among experiences; austerities hold only through true knowledge.
1659.nuance: Line 3, போகத்துள் போக்கியம், is obscure: it may mean that both kinds of austerity only yield experiences to be consumed, so neither frees without சத்திய ஞானம். The first line's claim is plain; the rest is my best reading.

1660.reading: The false garb is worn for the sake of eating; those who wear the true garb receive alms; but though the false garb be worn just like the true, a garb becomes one that saves only for those who have understood and known.
1660.nuance: மிகு பிச்சை கைக்கொள்வர் may mean the true wearers take alms as the highest thing, or simply that they live by alms rather than by feasting. The last two lines can be read as saying even an outwardly false garb saves the knower, or that no garb saves anyone but the knower; either way knowledge, not the garb, decides.

links.note: Both condemn those who live by others while posing as renouncers: the Kural calls none more hard-eyed than they, Tirumular says the show of devotion they put on for food finds no feet of Siva.
241 says the land withers when the unawakened take up tuft and thread and that it is good to cut them off; 1656 repeats the harm, adding famine, and calls stripping the garb of the base a joy.
Both put the world's welfare on the ruler's daily scrutiny (நாள்தோறும் நாடுக, நாடி நாடோறும): the Kural of those who do his work, Tirumular of all his people's conduct.
240 says the garb is true only for those who keep its way; 1660 restates the distinction of false and true garb and puts the test in knowledge.

source_issues: 1656: line 3 reads பஞ்ச்மாம், a misprint for பஞ்சமாம்.
